quote: Theorem 2.7. Let X, Y be two independent random variables having density functions fX, fY, cumulative distribution functions FX, FY, survival functions F̄X, F̄Y, respectively. Let T be a random variable with density function h and distribution function H. T is independent of X, Y. Then if 1. X ≥rh Y and either X or Y is IRHR then X^T ≥rh Y^T. 2. X ≤hr Y and either X or Y is DHR then X^T ≤hr Y^T.
family: General random variables under a common independent random shock (T-power transformation, X^T in the sense of Ebrahimi et al.)
compared: X^T vs Y^T under common shock T

hypotheses.text: (1) X ≥rh Y and either X or Y is IRHR
(2) X ≤hr Y and either X or Y is DHR

ambiguity: 'X^T' denotes the shock-transformed variable; superscript-T notation.

quote: Theorem 2.8. Let X and Y be two random variables. If X ≤hr Y and X or Y is DHR, then X ≤disp Y.

hypotheses.text: X ≤hr Y and X or Y is DHR

ambiguity: Background result attributed to Shaked et al.

quote: Theorem 2.9. Let X and Y be two random variables. If X ≤hr Y and X or Y is DHR, then X ≤LU Y.

hypotheses.text: X ≤hr Y and X or Y is DHR

conclusion.direction: X ≤_LU Y (less-uncertainty order, strengthening of Ebrahimi et al. Thm 2.3)

quote: Theorem 3.1. Let X1,...,Xn (Y1,...,Yn) be the set of continuous independent random variables having Xi ~ Gum(µi, σ) (Yi ~ Gum(µi*, σ)), i = 1, 2,..., n. Then, if µi ≥ µi*, we have Xn:n ≥lr Yn:n.
family: Gumbel distribution Gum(µ,σ): F(x) = exp(−e^{−(x−µ)/σ}), location µ ∈ R, scale σ > 0; independent components
compared: maxima Xn:n vs Yn:n; componentwise location ordering

hypotheses.text: Xi ~ Gum(µi,σ), Yi ~ Gum(µi*,σ) independent; common σ

quote: Theorem 3.2. Let X1,...,Xn (Y1,...,Yn) be the set of continuous independent random variables having Xi ~ Gum(µi, σ) (Yi ~ Gum(µi*, σ)), i = 1, 2,..., n. Then, if (µ1,...,µn) ≻m (µ1*,...,µn*), we have Xn:n ≥rh Yn:n.
compared: maxima Xn:n vs Yn:n; majorization of location vectors

hypotheses.formal: µ majorizes µ* (µ more spread); reversed hazard of maximum is Schur-convex in µ

quote: Corollary 3.3. Let X1,...,Xn (Y1,...,Yn) be the set of continuous independent random variables having Xi ~ Gum(µi, σ) (Yi ~ Gum(µi, σ)), i = 1, 2,..., n. Then, if (µ1,...,µn) ≻m (µ1*,...,µn*), and let T be any random variable which is independent of X and Y. Then we have Xn:n^T ≥rh Yn:n^T.

hypotheses.text: µ ≻m µ*; T independent of X and Y; Xn:n is IRHR

ambiguity: Statement prints Yi ~ Gum(µi, σ) (no asterisk) — presumed typo for µi*.

quote: Theorem 3.4. Let X1,...,Xn (Y1,...,Yn) be the set of continuous independent random variables having Xi ~ Gum(µi, σ) (Yi ~ Gum(µi*, σ)), i = 1, 2,..., n. Then, if (µ1,...,µn) ≻m (µ1*,...,µn*), we have X1:n ≤hr Y1:n.
compared: minima X1:n vs Y1:n; majorization of location vectors

hypotheses.formal: µ majorizes µ*; hazard rate of minimum is Schur-convex in µ

quote: Corollary 3.5. Let X1,...,Xn (Y1,...,Yn) be the set of continuous independent random variables having Xi ~ Gum(µi, σ) (Yi ~ Gum(µi*, σ)), i = 1, 2,..., n. Then, if (µ1,...,µn) ≻m (µ1*,...,µn*), and let T be any random variable which is independent of X and Y. Then we have X1:n^T ≤hr Y1:n^T.

hypotheses.text: µ ≻m µ*; T independent; X1:n is DHR (hazard rate decreasing in µi)

quote: Theorem 3.6. Let X1,...,Xn (Y1,...,Yn) be the set of continuous independent random variables having Xi ~ Gum(µi, σ) (Yi ~ Gum(µi*, σ)), i = 1, 2,..., n. Then, if (µ1,...,µn) ≻m (µ1*,...,µn*), we have 1. X1:n ≤disp Y1:n; 2. X1:n ≤LU Y1:n.

hypotheses.text: Xi ~ Gum(µi,σ), Yi ~ Gum(µi*,σ) independent; µ ≻m µ*

ambiguity: Two conclusions: dispersive order and less-uncertainty (LU) order, both via hr + DHR (Theorems 2.8, 2.9).
